title: Why Zelensky Poses a Unique Threat to Putin

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是Benjamin Poulin，我是Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《重塑者》（The Reframers），这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《重塑者》。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的Michael Barbaro。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》（The Daily）。

sentences.en: President Zelensky has stood down and stood up to and stared down President Putin.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基总统挺身而出，直面并蔑视了普京总统。

sentences.en: President Putin must be astounded, must be surprised, must be really disappointed.
sentences.zh: 普京总统一定感到震惊，一定感到意外，也一定非常失望。

sentences.en: Since the start of the war in Ukraine, no single figure has antagonized Vladimir Putin as effectively or persistently as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.
sentences.zh: 自乌克兰战争爆发以来，没有任何人能像乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基那样，如此有效且持久地对抗弗拉基米尔·普京。

sentences.en: Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky has emerged as a hero in his nation and around the world.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰的弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基已经成为他国家乃至全世界心目中的英雄。

sentences.en: Whose defiant videos and speeches have inspired the West and, by his own account, made him the target of assassination by Russia.
sentences.zh: 他那充满反抗精神的视频和演讲激励了西方，据他自己所说，这也让他成为了俄罗斯暗杀的目标。

sentences.en: Zelensky says he is Russia's number one military target and that his family is number two.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基表示，他是俄罗斯头号军事目标，而他的家人是二号目标。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, Moscow Bureau Chief Anton Trojanovsky, explains exactly what it is about Zelensky and his rise to power that poses such a unique threat to Putin.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事、莫斯科分社社长Anton Trojanovsky将详细解释泽连斯基及其崛起之路为何对普京构成了如此独特的威胁。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, March 8th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月8日，星期二。

sentences.en: Anton, how did you first get to know Volodymyr Zelensky?
sentences.zh: Anton，你是怎么开始了解弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基的？

sentences.en: I got to know him the way most people in both Russia and Ukraine got to know him, which is watching his stuff on TV.
sentences.zh: 我和俄罗斯及乌克兰的大多数人一样，是通过电视节目认识他的。

sentences.en: He had this Saturday Night Live type show on Ukrainian TV that started airing in 2005.
sentences.zh: 他在乌克兰电视台上有一档类似《周六夜现场》的节目，从2005年开始播出。

sentences.en: And he also had, of course, his breakout hit sitcom called Servant of the People, which first aired in 2015, in which he plays a schoolteacher.
sentences.zh: 当然，他还有一部成名作情景喜剧《人民公仆》，于2015年首播，他在剧中饰演一名学校老师。

sentences.en: Who suddenly goes viral on social media and becomes the president of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这位老师在社交媒体上突然走红，并最终成为了乌克兰总统。

sentences.en: And you can imagine that hilarity ensues.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象，这其中引发了多少令人捧腹的趣事。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So tell me more about this show.
sentences.zh: 那么，再多跟我讲讲这部剧吧。

sentences.en: It's this show that, you know, combines kind of the feel-good, we're-doing-the-right-thing attitude of the West Wing with the this-is-how-the-sausages-made comedy of Veep.
sentences.zh: 这部剧结合了《白宫风云》那种让人感觉良好、坚持做正确之事的态度，以及《副总统》那种揭露政治内幕的喜剧风格。

sentences.en: One of the most famous moments in the show is where he is negotiating with an official from the International Monetary Fund.
sentences.zh: 剧中有一个最著名的桥段，是他与国际货币基金组织（IMF）的一名官员进行谈判。

sentences.en: Where the IMF is trying to force Ukraine to meet all these conditions in order to get a loan that it needs.
sentences.zh: 当时IMF正试图强迫乌克兰满足各种条件，以获得所需的贷款。

sentences.en: And Zelensky goes out with this IMF official to a press conference facing journalists and cameras.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基带着这位IMF官员出席新闻发布会，面对着记者和摄像机。

sentences.en: And instead of giving the usual political lines about, you know, how we're going to be constructive, etc., Zelensky just says in Russian...
sentences.zh: 他没有说那些关于“我们将如何具有建设性”之类的官话，而是用俄语直接说道……

sentences.en: What I want to say is, you guys can go to hell to the IMF.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，你们这些IMF的人可以滚蛋了。

sentences.en: And Anton, why was a show about a Ukrainian politician, an accidental Ukrainian politician, something you were watching in Russia and sounds like became a hit within Russia?
sentences.zh: Anton，为什么一部关于乌克兰政客——一个意外成为政客的人——的剧集，会在俄罗斯引起关注，听起来甚至在俄罗斯也成了热门剧？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, the show was in Russian.
sentences.zh: 首先，这部剧是用俄语拍摄的。

sentences.en: Zelensky's a native Russian speaker, and that was the language that he used in his early, and in fact, through most of his career in show business.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基的母语是俄语，这也是他在演艺生涯早期，实际上几乎整个职业生涯中使用的语言。

sentences.en: Zelensky grew up in the Soviet Union in a working-class Russian-speaking city in southeastern Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基在苏联长大，出生在乌克兰东南部一个以俄语为主的工人阶级城市。

sentences.en: And, you know, in the decades after the collapse of the Soviet Union, the kind of entertainment market of Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Kazakhstan, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在苏联解体后的几十年里，俄罗斯、乌克兰、白俄罗斯、哈萨克斯坦的娱乐市场，你知道，

sentences.en: the whole Russian-speaking former Soviet Union remained very much intertwined.
sentences.zh: 整个讲俄语的前苏联地区在很大程度上仍然是相互交织的。

sentences.en: Zelensky actually spent a lot of his early career in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基其实在职业生涯早期在莫斯科待过很长时间。

sentences.en: He toured as a comedian.
sentences.zh: 他曾作为喜剧演员四处巡演。

sentences.en: He toured all around Russia and the former Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 他在俄罗斯和前苏联各地都进行过巡演。

sentences.en: And, you know, obviously, if you're a Ukrainian comedian, you're probably looking to break into the Russian market because it's much bigger.
sentences.zh: 而且，很显然，如果你是一名乌克兰喜剧演员，你很可能会寻求进入俄罗斯市场，因为那里的市场规模大得多。

sentences.en: So, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，

sentences.en: I think the fact that his show was popular in Russia as well as in Ukraine kind of showed how those countries remained intertwined culturally even after they started drifting apart politically in the early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 我认为他的剧在俄罗斯和乌克兰同样受欢迎，这在某种程度上表明，即使在21世纪初两国政治上开始分道扬镳之后，它们在文化上依然保持着紧密的联系。

sentences.en: That's really interesting.
sentences.zh: 这真的很有趣。

sentences.en: Did the Russian-Ukrainian relationship ever appear within this show?
sentences.zh: 这部剧中是否出现过俄乌关系的相关内容？

sentences.en: It did.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: You know, certainly the complicated issues of language and identity in Ukraine very much did.
sentences.zh: 你知道，乌克兰在语言和身份认同方面的复杂问题确实在剧中有所体现。

sentences.en: You know, there's this memorable moment where, so Zelensky's character in the show, this schoolteacher, Holoborotko, is a Russian speaker.
sentences.zh: 有一个令人难忘的片段，泽连斯基饰演的角色，那位学校老师Holoborotko，是个俄语使用者。

sentences.en: And then he gets into office and he suddenly has to learn Ukrainian because, you know, Ukrainian politicians are expected to speak Ukrainian in public.
sentences.zh: 后来他当选了，突然不得不学习乌克兰语，因为乌克兰政客在公开场合被要求讲乌克兰语。

sentences.en: And then, you know, there's some humorous moments in which he's trying to learn the language and messing up the words.
sentences.zh: 于是，剧中出现了一些幽默的桥段，他试图学习这门语言却总是说错词。

sentences.en: So, yeah, you know, that kind of issue of Ukrainian identity was also something that he lampooned a bit in his show.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，那种关于乌克兰身份认同的问题，也是他在剧中讽刺过的内容。

sentences.en: So, if you're a Russian TV consumer like, say, you, Anton, it would be easy to identify with Zelensky and his character on the show,
sentences.zh: 那么，如果你是一个像你这样的俄罗斯电视观众，Anton，是不是很容易对泽连斯基和他在剧中的角色产生共鸣？

sentences.en: and it sounds like the show itself is reinforcing the idea that there's a kinship between Ukraine and Russia.
sentences.zh: 而且听起来这部剧本身也在强化乌克兰和俄罗斯之间存在亲缘关系的想法。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, the show itself is not really all that much about the relationship between Ukraine and Russia.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，这部剧本身并不是真的在探讨乌克兰和俄罗斯之间的关系。

sentences.en: But if you look at the show kind of as a cultural object, you do see that, yes, you know,
sentences.zh: 但如果你把这部剧看作一个文化产品，你会发现，是的，你知道，

sentences.en: Zelensky himself owes much of his career to Russia and the Russian market and the economic benefits of being successful in such a big country.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基个人的职业生涯很大程度上归功于俄罗斯、俄罗斯市场，以及在一个如此庞大的国家取得成功所带来的经济利益。

sentences.en: The show itself is in Russian.
sentences.zh: 这部剧本身就是俄语的。

sentences.en: So, yes, it's, you know, it's something that in this region, it's kind of almost unsaid.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，在这个地区，这几乎是一种心照不宣的事实。

sentences.en: Like, yes, there are so many cultural and linguistic connections still between the countries of the former Soviet Union and certainly between Russia and Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 就像，是的，前苏联国家之间，尤其是俄罗斯和乌克兰之间，仍然存在着如此多的文化和语言联系。

sentences.en: But that does not, of course, necessarily mean that they have to have a political kinship as well.
sentences.zh: 但这当然并不意味着它们在政治上也必须拥有亲缘关系。

sentences.en: Right, but enough of a connection for this show to be a success.
sentences.zh: 没错，但这种联系足以让这部剧取得成功。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全如此。

sentences.en: And, you know, between this show and Zelensky's clips on his Variety show going viral on YouTube, he became a star in Russia as well as in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，通过这部剧以及泽连斯基在综艺节目中的片段在YouTube上疯传，他不仅在乌克兰，在俄罗斯也成了明星。

sentences.en: So then how does it come to pass that this very successful actor runs for president of Ukraine?
sentences.zh: 那么，这位非常成功的演员是如何走上竞选乌克兰总统之路的呢？

sentences.en: So this was 2019.
sentences.zh: 那是2019年的事了。

sentences.en: In fact, he announced his candidacy on the New Year's Eve edition of his show, December 31st, 2018.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他在2018年12月31日的新年特别节目中宣布了参选。

sentences.en: So then he runs for president.
sentences.zh: 于是他参加了总统竞选。

sentences.en: I remember visiting Kiev at the time and talking to Western diplomats who were all feverishly catching up on his TV show, telling me, this is just so strange.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时去基辅，和西方外交官交谈，他们都在疯狂地补看他的电视剧，并对我说，这真是太奇怪了。

sentences.en: You know, it's becoming so hard to tell what's fact and what's fiction.
sentences.zh: 你知道，现在越来越难分辨什么是现实，什么是虚构了。

sentences.en: Zelensky is making good on his promise to turn Ukrainian politics upside down.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基正在兑现他颠覆乌克兰政坛的承诺。

sentences.en: The campaign has been extraordinary, not least because Mr. Zelensky has avoided almost all of the things that candidates normally do in elections.
sentences.zh: 这场竞选非常不寻常，尤其是因为泽连斯基先生几乎避开了候选人在选举中通常会做的所有事情。

sentences.en: Just as an example, in the TV show,
sentences.zh: 举个例子，在电视剧里，

sentences.en: Zelensky's character as he's running for president takes to addressing voters doing these selfie videos and recording himself talking to regular Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基饰演的角色在竞选总统时，开始通过自拍视频向选民喊话，记录自己与普通乌克兰人的对话。

sentences.en: And then Zelensky's real life presidential campaign videos take a similar style and are also interspersed with clips from Servant of the People, the show.
sentences.zh: 然后，泽连斯基现实生活中的总统竞选视频也采用了类似的风格，并且穿插了《人民公仆》剧中的片段。

sentences.en: So, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的。

sentences.en: This is very, very meta.
sentences.zh: 这非常、非常具有元叙事色彩。

sentences.en: It was very meta.
sentences.zh: 确实非常具有元叙事色彩。

sentences.en: His campaign has barely existed in real life.
sentences.zh: 他的竞选活动在现实生活中几乎不存在。

sentences.en: The only time the candidates have publicly exchanged views, by phone, it was a disaster.
sentences.zh: 候选人唯一一次公开交换意见是通过电话，结果是一场灾难。

sentences.en: Also, by the way, Zelensky's political party is called Servant of the People, as in the name of his TV show.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，泽连斯基的政党也叫“人民公仆”，和他的电视剧名字一样。

sentences.en: It's as if Martin Sheen ran for president and registered a party called the West Wing.
sentences.zh: 这就好比马丁·辛（Martin Sheen）竞选总统，并注册了一个叫《白宫风云》的政党。

sentences.en: We don't know how serious Zelensky was, of course, when he first ran.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们不知道泽连斯基最初参选时有多认真。

sentences.en: But the fact is, he proved remarkably successful as a candidate, you know, because he just had such a fresh approach to politics, such a youthful approach.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，他作为候选人表现得非常成功，因为他给政治带来了一种非常新鲜、非常年轻的方法。

sentences.en: It was such a contrast to kind of the staid and many believed corrupt political establishment of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 这与乌克兰那种沉闷且被许多人认为腐败的政治体制形成了鲜明对比。

sentences.en: It was a really remarkable rise that he had.
sentences.zh: 他的崛起确实非常引人注目。

sentences.en: Well, explain that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，解释一下。

sentences.en: What were his key messages in that 2019 campaign?
sentences.zh: 他在2019年竞选中的核心主张是什么？

sentences.en: Well, one, which was very popular, was opposing corruption, promising to be more running, a more honest and clean government.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中一个非常受欢迎的主张是反对腐败，承诺建立一个更诚实、更廉洁的政府。

sentences.en: And then the second one was to end the war in eastern Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 第二个主张是结束乌克兰东部的战争。

sentences.en: Zelensky really drew a contrast with Petro Poroshenko, the incumbent.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基确实与现任总统彼得·波罗申科形成了鲜明对比。

sentences.en: Poroshenko was someone with very close ties in western governments.
sentences.zh: 波罗申科与西方政府有着非常密切的关系。

sentences.en: And so Zelensky came in drawing a contrast to that.
sentences.zh: 所以泽连斯基的出现与此形成了对比。

sentences.en: Zelensky talked about wanting to sit down with Putin directly and make a deal.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基谈到希望直接与普京坐下来达成协议。

sentences.en: You know, he signaled that he could be willing to compromise with Putin to basically stop the dying there in Ukraine's war with Russian-backed separatists.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他暗示自己愿意与普京妥协，以基本停止乌克兰与俄罗斯支持的分离主义者之间的战争所带来的伤亡。

sentences.en: And that was something that actually at the time made a lot of western diplomats and others nervous.
sentences.zh: 这在当时确实让许多西方外交官和其他人感到紧张。

sentences.en: People thought that Zelensky might end up being too soft on Putin and lacked the experience to really be able to take him on.
sentences.zh: 人们认为泽连斯基最终可能会对普京太软弱，并且缺乏真正能够对抗他的经验。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: This is a fascinating piece of information in retrospect, that Zelensky's campaign for president made people think that he could be quite close to Putin and to Russia.
sentences.zh: 回想起来，这是一个令人着迷的信息：泽连斯基的总统竞选曾让人认为他可能与普京和俄罗斯走得很近。

sentences.en: Yes, you know, Zelensky ran with no political experience, certainly with no foreign policy experience.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，泽连斯基在没有任何政治经验，当然也没有任何外交政策经验的情况下参加了竞选。

sentences.en: I remember I was there at one of his first meetings with foreign correspondents.
sentences.zh: 我记得我当时在他与外国记者的第一次会面现场。

sentences.en: We asked him, so what are you going to do?
sentences.zh: 我们问他，你打算怎么做？

sentences.en: How are you actually going to end the war?
sentences.zh: 你到底打算如何结束这场战争？

sentences.en: And he didn't have any specific idea.
sentences.zh: 他没有任何具体的想法。

sentences.en: He spoke about sort of the idea that, well, if he were to be able to sit down with Putin man to man, that they'd be able to make a deal and finally end this.
sentences.zh: 他谈到了一种想法，即如果他能与普京面对面坐下来，他们就能达成协议，最终结束这一切。

sentences.en: So there was a lot of skepticism that Zelensky was the right man for the job, in particular when it came to foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们对泽连斯基是否是这份工作的合适人选存在很多怀疑，特别是在外交政策方面。

sentences.en: But in the broader public, that message of ending the war was extremely popular.
sentences.zh: 但在广大公众中，结束战争的信息非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: And it was even popular in the more Russia-friendly corners of Ukraine in the south and in the east,
sentences.zh: 甚至在乌克兰南部和东部那些对俄罗斯更友好的地区也很受欢迎，

sentences.en: where people sort of were positive about the idea of kind of rebuilding some ties to Russia.
sentences.zh: 那里的人们对重建与俄罗斯的一些联系持积极态度。

sentences.en: So there we have it.
sentences.zh: 所以情况就是这样。

sentences.en: Fact is following it.
sentences.zh: 事实紧随其后。

sentences.en: He's going to become Ukraine's real president.
sentences.zh: 他将成为乌克兰真正的总统。

sentences.en: A 41-year-old actor and comedian with no political experience whatsoever has won today's presidential election in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 一位没有任何政治经验的41岁演员兼喜剧演员赢得了今天乌克兰的总统大选。

sentences.en: He wins in a blowout, 73% of the vote.
sentences.zh: 他以压倒性优势获胜，获得了73%的选票。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So just to recap, at the moment Zelensky becomes Ukraine's president, overwhelmingly, given that vote tally,
sentences.zh: 所以简单回顾一下，在泽连斯基成为乌克兰总统的那一刻，鉴于投票结果，他是以压倒性优势当选的，

sentences.en: his relationship to Russia is as a celebrity within Russia because of his television shows and a celebrity within Russia who has communicated that he thinks some form of peace with Putin and a good working relationship with Putin is possible.
sentences.zh: 他与俄罗斯的关系是作为俄罗斯家喻户晓的明星，因为他的电视节目，而且他曾表示认为与普京达成某种形式的和平以及建立良好的工作关系是可能的。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: So did Putin welcome Zelensky's victory?
sentences.zh: 那么普京欢迎泽连斯基的胜利吗？

sentences.en: It would seem like he would.
sentences.zh: 看起来他应该是欢迎的。

sentences.en: There was optimism in Russia, certainly.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯国内确实存在乐观情绪。

sentences.en: I mean, you could see it in the polls when people were asked their views on Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你可以从民调中看出来，当人们被问及对乌克兰的看法时，

sentences.en: It really, there was a big jump upward.
sentences.zh: 确实有一个很大的提升。

sentences.en: And in the Kremlin, yes, also.
sentences.zh: 在克里姆林宫，是的，也是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, the reaction was more muted.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，反应比较低调。

sentences.en: But clearly, there was an idea there, too, that this was a guy that they could work with, someone who might be, you know, in the Kremlin's kind of conspiratorial thinking,
sentences.zh: 但很明显，那里也有一个想法，即这是一个他们可以合作的人，一个可能——你知道，在克里姆林宫那种阴谋论思维中——

sentences.en: a guy who is less dependent on the West and might act more independently.
sentences.zh: 一个不太依赖西方、可能行动更独立的人。

sentences.en: So when does Zelensky's relationship with Russia as president start to change?
sentences.zh: 那么泽连斯基作为总统与俄罗斯的关系是从什么时候开始改变的？

sentences.en: I think it starts to change pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 我认为改变得相当快。

sentences.en: In that first year, 2019, he meets with Putin in person at the end of 2019 in Paris.
sentences.zh: 在第一年，即2019年，他于2019年底在巴黎与普京进行了面对面会晤。

sentences.en: You know, they try to get some peace talks off the ground, but it becomes clear pretty quickly, especially sort of as the pandemic comes around in 2020,
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们试图启动一些和平谈判，但很快就变得很清楚，特别是在2020年疫情到来之后，

sentences.en: that it is much easier said than done that you're going to make a deal with Russia.
sentences.zh: 与俄罗斯达成协议说起来容易做起来难。

sentences.en: And you could really see Zelensky becoming more and more frustrated.
sentences.zh: 你可以真正看到泽连斯基变得越来越沮丧。

sentences.en: You know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，

sentences.en: there was one of the first points of tension where you could see there was a fork in the road and Zelensky went a certain direction was when Russia was offering its Sputnik coronavirus vaccine to Ukraine,
sentences.zh: 最初的紧张点之一，你可以看到这里有一个分岔路口，而泽连斯基选择了一个特定的方向，那就是当俄罗斯向乌克兰提供其“卫星-V”新冠疫苗时，

sentences.en: which would have been a huge PR victory for the Kremlin if Zelensky had agreed to it.
sentences.zh: 如果泽连斯基同意了，那将是克里姆林宫的一场巨大的公关胜利。

sentences.en: And he did not.
sentences.zh: 但他没有。

sentences.en: He refused to do it.
sentences.zh: 他拒绝了。

sentences.en: He held out for Western vaccines.
sentences.zh: 他坚持等待西方疫苗。

sentences.en: So that was one early sign of Zelensky taking a pro-Western route and being skeptical, being cautious of getting too close to Russia.
sentences.zh: 所以这是泽连斯基采取亲西方路线，并对与俄罗斯走得太近持怀疑和谨慎态度的早期迹象。

sentences.en: And then he became more outspoken about wanting to join the NATO alliance.
sentences.zh: 然后，他开始更直言不讳地表示希望加入北约联盟。

sentences.en: Which, of course, as we now know, is seen as the ultimate act of provocation toward Putin's Russia because he sees NATO as such a threat to his authority and his power.
sentences.zh: 当然，正如我们现在所知，这被视为对普京的俄罗斯的终极挑衅行为，因为他将北约视为对其权威和权力的巨大威胁。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I should add that in addition to being frustrated with Russia, Zelensky was also seeing an increasingly receptive attitude in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 我应该补充一点，除了对俄罗斯感到沮丧外，泽连斯基在西方也看到了越来越积极的态度。

sentences.en: You know, Zelensky was elected in 2019 when Donald Trump was president,
sentences.zh: 你知道，泽连斯基是在2019年唐纳德·特朗普担任总统时当选的，

sentences.en: a man who was not all that interested in helping Ukraine take a pro-Western path and also was not all that critical of President Putin.
sentences.zh: 那个人对帮助乌克兰走上亲西方道路并不怎么感兴趣，对普京总统也不怎么批评。

sentences.en: But then Biden becomes president, and he comes in, of course,
sentences.zh: 但后来拜登当选总统，他上任时，当然，

sentences.en: with a message of much greater support for Ukraine to take a path that brings it closer to Western institutions and takes it farther away from Russia.
sentences.zh: 带着更大的支持力度，鼓励乌克兰走上一条使其更接近西方机构、远离俄罗斯的道路。

sentences.en: So what happens is just days after Biden is inaugurated, Zelensky cracks down on a business tycoon in Ukraine named Viktor Medvedchuk.
sentences.zh: 所以发生的事情是，就在拜登就职几天后，泽连斯基对乌克兰的一位商业大亨维克多·梅德韦丘克采取了行动。

sentences.en: And that's important because Medvedchuk is basically the closest link remaining between Ukraine and the Kremlin.
sentences.zh: 这一点很重要，因为梅德韦丘克基本上是乌克兰与克里姆林宫之间仅存的最紧密联系。

sentences.en: Putin is the godfather of Medvedchuk's daughter.
sentences.zh: 普京是梅德韦丘克女儿的教父。

sentences.en: Medvedchuk runs a political party that is fairly pro-Russian.
sentences.zh: 梅德韦丘克经营着一个相当亲俄的政党。

sentences.en: He was running several TV channels that were pro-Russian.
sentences.zh: 他经营着几家亲俄的电视频道。

sentences.en: And early last year, Zelensky closes those TV channels, starts an investigation into Medvedchuk.
sentences.zh: 去年年初，泽连斯基关闭了这些电视频道，并开始对梅德韦丘克进行调查。

sentences.en: Last May, Medvedchuk was put under house arrest under suspicion of treason.
sentences.zh: 去年五月，梅德韦丘克因涉嫌叛国罪被软禁。

sentences.en: So Zelensky took all these steps that were very aggressive.
sentences.zh: 所以泽连斯基采取了一系列非常激进的措施。

sentences.en: And that was something that clearly annoyed Putin greatly.
sentences.zh: 这显然让普京感到非常恼火。

sentences.en: And in retrospect, was likely one of the factors that exacerbated the situation between Ukraine and Russia.
sentences.zh: 回想起来，这很可能是加剧乌克兰和俄罗斯之间局势的因素之一。

sentences.en: So Anton, you're saying the shift in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以安东，你的意思是美国总统从特朗普换成拜登，

sentences.en: presidency from Trump to Biden represented to Zelensky that he had more Western support and that basically he had some backup if he wanted to cross Putin.
sentences.zh: 对泽连斯基来说意味着他获得了更多的西方支持，如果他想对抗普京，基本上有了后盾。

sentences.en: And so it's then that he starts taking more and more aggressive steps to move away from Russia.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，他开始采取越来越激进的措施来远离俄罗斯。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And as his presidency progressed, he found himself more and more on a collision course with Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 随着总统任期的推进，他发现自己与弗拉基米尔·普京的冲突愈演愈烈。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无保留、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Anton, what happens next is pretty well known.
sentences.zh: 安东，接下来发生的事情大家都知道了。

sentences.en: Putin becomes more and more inflamed by Zelensky and by the possibility, however remote, that under Zelensky, Ukraine might end up joining NATO.
sentences.zh: 普京对泽连斯基感到越来越愤怒，也对泽连斯基领导下的乌克兰最终可能加入北约的可能性（尽管微乎其微）感到恼火。

sentences.en: Putin begins amassing more and more troops on Ukraine's borders and eventually, of course, invading Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 普京开始在乌克兰边境集结越来越多的军队，当然，最终入侵了乌克兰。

sentences.en: Given everything that you just told us, what stood out to you about how Zelensky responded to that?
sentences.zh: 鉴于你刚才告诉我们的一切，泽连斯基对此作出的反应中，有什么让你印象深刻的地方？

sentences.en: Well, Zelensky responds showing himself as a master communicator, you know,
sentences.zh: 嗯，泽连斯基展现出了他作为沟通大师的一面，你知道，

sentences.en: showing his knowledge of how to get the gravity of the moment across in a moment of crisis that in some ways recalls his TV show.
sentences.zh: 他展现了自己如何在一个危机时刻传达出事态的严重性，这在某种程度上让人想起他的电视节目。

sentences.en: You know, remember, we were talking about the selfie videos that he was doing as a presidential candidate on his sitcom and then as a real life presidential candidate.
sentences.zh: 记得吗，我们之前谈到过他作为总统候选人在情景喜剧中，以及后来作为现实生活中的总统候选人时拍摄的自拍视频。

sentences.en: And recently, he's been doing selfie videos from a city under siege.
sentences.zh: 最近，他一直在被围困的城市里拍摄自拍视频。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, in a T-shirt, unshaven, showing his people that he's there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，穿着T恤，没刮胡子，向他的人民展示他就在那里。

sentences.en: He hasn't fled.
sentences.zh: 他没有逃跑。

sentences.en: He's ready to defend his country.
sentences.zh: 他准备保卫自己的国家。

sentences.en: And importantly, too, he's not just speaking to the Ukrainian people.
sentences.zh: 而且重要的是，他不仅是在对乌克兰人民说话。

sentences.en: He's speaking to the Russian people.
sentences.zh: 他是在对俄罗斯人民说话。

sentences.en: Remember, I mentioned that whole bid in his TV show where he's a Russian speaker trying to learn Ukrainian because Ukrainian officials are expected to speak Ukrainian in public.
sentences.zh: 记得我提到过他电视节目里的那个桥段吗？他扮演一个讲俄语的人，努力学习乌克兰语，因为乌克兰官员在公共场合被要求讲乌克兰语。

sentences.en: Well, recently, he's doing public addresses in Russian.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最近，他开始用俄语发表公开演讲。

sentences.en: He's been speaking his native Russian in order to reach Russians directly.
sentences.zh: 他一直在用他的母语俄语说话，以便直接接触俄罗斯人。

sentences.en: And the first such address was the night of February 23rd, in the early morning of the 24th, hours before Russia launched its attack.
sentences.zh: 第一次这样的演讲是在2月23日晚上，也就是24日凌晨，在俄罗斯发动袭击前几个小时。

sentences.en: Zelensky posted a video to social media saying,
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基在社交媒体上发布了一段视频，说道：

sentences.en: I'm coming to you, to citizens of Russia, speaking your language,
sentences.zh: “我向你们，俄罗斯公民，用你们的语言说话，”

sentences.en: describing his attachment to Ukraine and really trying to counter Putin's fundamental message that Ukraine isn't even a real country.
sentences.zh: 他描述了自己对乌克兰的依恋，并试图反驳普京关于“乌克兰甚至不是一个真正的国家”这一根本论调。

sentences.en: So, he says, for instance, you are told that this flame, referring to the war, will bring freedom to the Ukrainian people.
sentences.zh: 例如，他说，有人告诉你们，这团火焰（指战争）会给乌克兰人民带来自由。

sentences.en: But the people of Ukraine are already free.
sentences.zh: 但乌克兰人民已经是自由的了。

sentences.en: Hear our voices.
sentences.zh: 听听我们的声音。

sentences.en: We want peace.
sentences.zh: 我们想要和平。

sentences.en: And he ends the speech by saying,
sentences.zh: 他在演讲结束时问道：

sentences.en: Do the people of Russia want war, he asks?
sentences.zh: “俄罗斯人民想要战争吗？”

sentences.en: I would like to be able to answer this.
sentences.zh: “我希望能回答这个问题。”

sentences.en: But the answer depends only on you, the citizens of the Russian Federation.
sentences.zh: “但答案只取决于你们，俄罗斯联邦的公民。”

sentences.en: So, he's telling Russians that Ukraine is not a threat to them, that even though these countries share all these ties,
sentences.zh: 所以，他在告诉俄罗斯人，乌克兰对他们没有威胁，尽管这些国家有着千丝万缕的联系，

sentences.en: that doesn't mean, essentially, that Russia needs to invade the Ukraine in order to secure those ties.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着俄罗斯必须入侵乌克兰才能巩固这些联系。

sentences.en: You know, Putin's argument, as you know, is Ukrainians and Russians are one people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，普京的论点是，乌克兰人和俄罗斯人是一个民族。

sentences.en: Putin claims that the West is controlling Ukraine, that the West is using Ukraine as, you know, a platform to attack Russia,
sentences.zh: 普京声称西方正在控制乌克兰，西方正在利用乌克兰作为攻击俄罗斯的平台，

sentences.en: basically taking away any agency from the Ukrainian people.
sentences.zh: 这基本上剥夺了乌克兰人民的任何自主权。

sentences.en: And here's Zelensky himself in Russia saying,
sentences.zh: 而泽连斯基亲自用俄语回应说：

sentences.en: No, that's not true.
sentences.zh: 不，那不是真的。

sentences.en: Ukraine has made its own decision.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰已经做出了自己的决定。

sentences.en: And despite all those ties, despite all that kinship that, of course, Zelensky himself and his personal story symbolizes,
sentences.zh: 尽管有所有的联系，尽管有泽连斯基本人和他的个人故事所象征的那种亲缘关系，

sentences.en: Ukraine has chosen a different path.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰选择了另一条道路。

sentences.en: That's Zelensky's basic argument.
sentences.zh: 这就是泽连斯基的基本论点。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's the attitude, it seems, of most Ukrainians and why they would be compelled to take up arms and fight so forcefully against Russia.
sentences.zh: 这似乎也是大多数乌克兰人的态度，也是他们为何被迫拿起武器，如此有力地反抗俄罗斯的原因。

sentences.en: But I'm wondering how Zelensky's message in this speech goes over with Russians.
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，泽连斯基在这次演讲中的信息在俄罗斯人中反响如何？

sentences.en: Well, in the hours after that first speech, the invasion happens.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在那次演讲后的几个小时里，入侵就开始了。

sentences.en: Russia starts to bomb Ukrainian targets and Russian tanks move across the border into Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯开始轰炸乌克兰目标，俄罗斯坦克越过边境进入乌克兰。

sentences.en: Zelensky's speech in Russian is ricocheting through Russian social media accounts.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基的俄语演讲在俄罗斯社交媒体账号上迅速传播。

sentences.en: People are clearly seeing that in the country.
sentences.zh: 人们显然在那个国家看到了这一点。

sentences.en: And then that first day, February 24th, Russians take to the streets.
sentences.zh: 然后在那第一天，2月24日，俄罗斯人走上了街头。

sentences.en: In dozens of cities across the country, there are thousands of arrests.
sentences.zh: 在全国几十个城市，有数千人被捕。

sentences.en: Of people who are doing things like chanting no to war on the streets of Moscow, St. Petersburg, and elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 这些人做的事情包括在莫斯科、圣彼得堡和其他地方的街头高喊“不要战争”。

sentences.en: Very much doing what Zelensky is, in a sense, asking them to do, oppose this war.
sentences.zh: 在某种意义上，他们非常符合泽连斯基对他们的要求：反对这场战争。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it's a very, I think, visceral feeling for many Russians that this war is an abomination.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为对于许多俄罗斯人来说，这是一种非常发自内心的感觉，即这场战争是一种罪恶。

sentences.en: And certainly hearing Zelensky address them, you know, you can't discount the influence of that either.
sentences.zh: 当然，听到泽连斯基对他们喊话，你也不能忽视其影响力。

sentences.en: So not long after that, Zelensky posts another one of these videos where he's basically saying thank you for hearing us to the Russian people.
sentences.zh: 所以在那之后不久，泽连斯基又发布了另一段视频，基本上是在对俄罗斯人民说“谢谢你们倾听我们”。

sentences.en: He says, to all the citizens of the Russian Federation who come out to protest, I want to say, we see you.
sentences.zh: 他说，对于所有走出来抗议的俄罗斯联邦公民，我想说，我们看到了你们。

sentences.en: This means that you heard us.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你们听到了我们的声音。

sentences.en: This means that you're beginning to trust us.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你们开始信任我们了。

sentences.en: Fight for us.
sentences.zh: 为我们而战。

sentences.en: Fight against the war.
sentences.zh: 反对这场战争。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So Zelensky's having a kind of running conversation with the Russian people, and knowing what you've told us about his celebrity within Russia, and how Russians feel about him,
sentences.zh: 所以泽连斯基正在与俄罗斯人民进行一种持续的对话，考虑到你告诉我们的他在俄罗斯的名气，以及俄罗斯人对他的感受，

sentences.en: that kind of running conversation must resonate in a unique and powerful way.
sentences.zh: 这种持续的对话一定会产生独特而强大的共鸣。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think for a certain segment of the population, his message is landing.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于一部分民众来说，他的信息正在产生影响。

sentences.en: And again, this isn't just a faceless president of another country.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这不仅仅是另一个国家的无名总统。

sentences.en: This is a film celebrity that a lot of people knew long before he became president.
sentences.zh: 这是一位在成为总统之前就被许多人熟知的电影明星。

sentences.en: And Zelensky becomes relentless about these communications.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基在这些沟通上变得锲而不舍。

sentences.en: In the days after the invasion, he's doing these speeches on video every day, multiple times a day.
sentences.zh: 入侵后的几天里，他每天都在视频中发表这些演讲，每天多次。

sentences.en: Of course, a lot of them are directed at Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中很多是针对乌克兰人的。

sentences.en: Some are directed at the West, where he's saying that the West needs to do more to help Ukraine financially and militarily.
sentences.zh: 有些是针对西方的，他表示西方需要做更多工作，在经济和军事上帮助乌克兰。

sentences.en: But he also continues to direct some of these dispatches at Russians, who he refers to at one point as peaceful people of a belligerent state.
sentences.zh: 但他同时也继续向俄罗斯人发布这些信息，他曾一度称他们为“好战国家的和平人民”。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯嗯。

sentences.en: It seems he's working very hard to separate the Russian people in this moment from their leader.
sentences.zh: 看来他正在非常努力地在这一刻将俄罗斯人民与他们的领导人区分开来。

sentences.en: He's saying, I'm speaking to you because Putin doesn't represent you.
sentences.zh: 他在说，我之所以对你们说话，是因为普京并不代表你们。

sentences.en: I mean, he's trying to drive a wedge between the leadership of Russia in this moment and the Russian people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他试图在这一刻在俄罗斯领导层和俄罗斯人民之间打入楔子。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So how does the leader of Russia, Vladimir Putin, and the Kremlin respond to these Zelensky communications?
sentences.zh: 那么俄罗斯领导人弗拉基米尔·普京和克里姆林宫对泽连斯基的这些沟通有何回应？

sentences.en: Well, Michael, their message is Zelensky is totally out of his depth.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，他们的信息是泽连斯基完全无法胜任。

sentences.en: They're saying he's controlled by Western puppet masters and what the Kremlin calls falsely Nazis in Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 他们说他受到西方傀儡操纵者的控制，以及克里姆林宫所称的乌克兰境内的“纳粹”。

sentences.en: Zelensky also keeps saying he wants to talk to Putin directly.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基也一直说他想直接与普京对话。

sentences.en: He wants to negotiate an end to the fighting while the Kremlin has been saying there's nothing to talk about.
sentences.zh: 他想通过谈判结束战斗，而克里姆林宫一直说没什么可谈的。

sentences.en: Sort of very dismissive of Zelensky as a leader and of the idea that he may have any influence.
sentences.zh: 这是一种对泽连斯基作为领导人的蔑视，也否定了他可能产生任何影响的想法。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯嗯。

sentences.en: And the fact is there are plenty of Russians who are willing to believe that narrative.
sentences.zh: 事实是，有许多俄罗斯人愿意相信这种叙事。

sentences.en: I was actually just, before we got on, looking at some of the comments on Russian social media about the Zelensky videos.
sentences.zh: 实际上，在我们开始录制之前，我正在查看俄罗斯社交媒体上关于泽连斯基视频的一些评论。

sentences.en: And one typical kind of comment is, oh, he's a great guy, cool, looks just like a typical Russian or Ukrainian working class man.
sentences.zh: 其中一种典型的评论是：哦，他是个好人，很酷，看起来就像一个典型的俄罗斯或乌克兰工人阶级男人。

sentences.en: But it's too bad that all those neo-Nazis have gotten to him.
sentences.zh: 但可惜的是，那些新纳粹分子已经控制了他。

sentences.en: That's the Kremlin propaganda breaking through.
sentences.zh: 这就是克里姆林宫的宣传正在渗透。

sentences.en: So we have to be cautious not to overstate, I think, the impact of the strategy that Zelensky has taken.
sentences.zh: 所以我们必须谨慎，我认为不要夸大泽连斯基所采取策略的影响。

sentences.en: Understood.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: But it is clear that Zelensky's message, especially to Russians, is getting under Vladimir Putin's skin.
sentences.zh: 但很明显，泽连斯基的信息，尤其是对俄罗斯人的信息，确实触动了弗拉基米尔·普京的神经。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I think it is.
sentences.zh: 我认为是的。

sentences.en: And I think that what Zelensky symbolizes is really an existential problem for the Kremlin,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为泽连斯基所象征的实际上是克里姆林宫的一个生存问题，

sentences.en: which is that he's someone steeped in the Russian-speaking culture of the post-Soviet space.
sentences.zh: 那就是他是一个深受后苏联空间俄语文化熏陶的人。

sentences.en: He comes from a Russian-speaking city in southeastern Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 他来自乌克兰东南部的一个讲俄语的城市。

sentences.en: And he's someone who has built his career on his appeal in Russia and elsewhere in the former Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 他凭借自己在俄罗斯和前苏联其他地区的影响力建立了职业生涯。

sentences.en: And despite all that, he wants to take his country on a pro-Western path and does not want to subjugate it to the dominance of Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他还是想带领自己的国家走上一条亲西方的道路，不想让它屈服于弗拉基米尔·普京的统治。

sentences.en: So that's what makes him such a potent symbol politically in the region across the former Soviet space and also, I think, makes him such a danger to Putin.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是他在整个前苏联地区的政治上成为如此强有力的象征的原因，我也认为这使他成为普京的巨大威胁。

sentences.en: And so is that why so many people believe that Putin wants Zelensky dead, wants to kill him?
sentences.zh: 那么这就是为什么这么多人认为普京想要泽连斯基死，想要杀掉他的原因吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, and, you know, Zelensky talks about it himself all the time.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且你知道，泽连斯基自己也一直在谈论这件事。

sentences.en: He makes that a big part of his communications.
sentences.zh: 他把这作为他沟通的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: Zelensky trying to show people that he's not afraid and trying to set an example, I think, for the people of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基试图向人们展示他不害怕，并试图为乌克兰人民树立一个榜样。

sentences.en: And also show to the Russian people watching him that he remains and the Ukrainian people remain defiant.
sentences.zh: 同时也向观看他的俄罗斯人民展示，他依然存在，乌克兰人民依然不屈不挠。

sentences.en: Right, and each one of these videos is also a way for Zelensky to say, quite simply, I'm still here, I'm still alive, I'm still in charge,
sentences.zh: 没错，这些视频中的每一个也是泽连斯基简单地表达“我还在这里，我还活着，我还在掌权”的一种方式，

sentences.en: which is itself a kind of provocation to Putin.
sentences.zh: 这本身就是对普京的一种挑衅。

sentences.en: Exactly, because, you know, the Russians, I think, if you listen to Russian state TV and to Russian politicians, they clearly expected him to flee as soon as the war began.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为你知道，如果你听俄罗斯国家电视台和俄罗斯政客的言论，他们显然预期他会在战争开始时就逃跑。

sentences.en: But I'm really curious, doesn't everything we're talking about here make Volodymyr Zelensky someone whose death might backfire on Putin?
sentences.zh: 但我真的很好奇，我们在这里谈论的一切难道不会让弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基的死反而对普京产生反作用吗？

sentences.en: Zelensky's deep connections to the Russian people, his effectiveness at communicating to both them and Ukrainians in this moment.
sentences.zh: 泽连斯基与俄罗斯人民的深厚联系，他在这一刻与他们以及乌克兰人沟通的有效性。

sentences.en: If Putin were to take Zelensky out, couldn't he then become a martyr and wouldn't that end up being bad for Putin?
sentences.zh: 如果普京除掉泽连斯基，他难道不会成为烈士，而这最终对普京不利吗？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, this war has already been so shocking in so many ways that we can't really make predictions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，这场战争在很多方面已经如此令人震惊，以至于我们无法做出预测。

sentences.en: And one of the things I think that's been shocking to the Kremlin is just how much of a determined and dignified leader Zelensky has emerged under this incredible pressure.
sentences.zh: 我认为令克里姆林宫感到震惊的事情之一，就是泽连斯基在这种难以置信的压力下展现出了多么坚定和尊严的领导力。

sentences.en: And so if Zelensky were to be killed, there would be a cost to Putin.
sentences.zh: 所以如果泽连斯基被杀，普京将付出代价。

sentences.en: He will have inspired Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 他将激励乌克兰人。

sentences.en: And I think just as importantly, he will have really, I think, succeeded in drawing this line between the Kremlin and the people of Russia, you know,
sentences.zh: 而且我认为同样重要的是，他确实成功地在克里姆林宫和俄罗斯人民之间划清了界限，你知道，

sentences.en: in this incredible position where his country is under fire, under attack from cruise missiles and artillery and tanks.
sentences.zh: 在他的国家处于战火之中，受到巡航导弹、火炮和坦克的攻击时，他处于这种不可思议的境地。

sentences.en: And even as that's happening, he's reaching out to the Russian people next door and saying, we still kind of understand you.
sentences.zh: 即使在这种情况发生时，他仍在向隔壁的俄罗斯人民伸出援手，说：我们仍然在某种程度上理解你们。

sentences.en: We don't throw you all into one pot with your leader.
sentences.zh: 我们不会把你们和你们的领导人混为一谈。

sentences.en: That message is resonating right now in this time of crisis.
sentences.zh: 这个信息在当前的危机时刻引起了共鸣。

sentences.en: And no matter what, live or die, that'll be a big part of Zelensky's legacy.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，无论生死，这都将是泽连斯基遗产的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: Anton, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 安东，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: On Monday night, in his latest self-recorded video, Zelensky spoke to Ukrainians from his presidential office in Kyiv, the first time he has appeared there since the war began.
sentences.zh: 周一晚上，在最新的自录视频中，泽连斯基在基辅的总统办公室向乌克兰人发表了讲话，这是自战争开始以来他首次在那里露面。

sentences.en: In remarks seemingly aimed at Putin, Zelensky declared that he was not afraid of anyone.
sentences.zh: 在似乎针对普京的言论中，泽连斯基宣称他不怕任何人。

sentences.en: And rebuked Russian forces for attacking civilian sites, including a bread factory.
sentences.zh: 并谴责俄罗斯军队袭击民用设施，包括一家面包厂。

sentences.en: Think about it, he said.
sentences.zh: 想想看，他说。

sentences.en: To fire at the bread factory.
sentences.zh: 向面包厂开火。

sentences.en: Who could you be to do that?
sentences.zh: 你得是什么样的人才会这样做？

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app, unlocked?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用，免费解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用一个月，且无需绑定信用卡，你会怎么做？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在机会来了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 首次下载《纽约时报》应用，即可免费畅享首月会员权益。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall, to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《纽约时报》订阅用户每天都能读到什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订阅用户，今天就下载应用，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On Monday, the state of Florida said it would recommend that healthy children not be vaccinated against COVID-19,
sentences.zh: 周一，佛罗里达州政府表示，建议健康儿童无需接种新冠疫苗，

sentences.en: directly contradicting guidance from federal health officials.
sentences.zh: 这直接违背了联邦卫生官员的指导意见。

sentences.en: The recommendation was approved by the state's controversial Surgeon General.
sentences.zh: 该建议由佛州备受争议的卫生局局长批准。

sentences.en: A Republican appointee who has expressed skepticism of the vaccine's effectiveness.
sentences.zh: 他是一位共和党任命的官员，曾对疫苗的有效性表示怀疑。

sentences.en: Is that a good policy?
sentences.zh: 这是项好政策吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 绝对不是。

sentences.en: Let me just note that...
sentences.zh: 我只想指出……

sentences.en: Asked about the decision, White House Press Secretary Jen Psaki expressed alarm,
sentences.zh: 当被问及这一决定时，白宫新闻秘书珍·普萨基表示震惊，

sentences.en: citing data that shows unvaccinated teenagers are far likelier to be hospitalized with COVID than vaccinated teenagers.
sentences.zh: 她援引数据指出，未接种疫苗的青少年因新冠住院的可能性远高于已接种疫苗的青少年。

sentences.en: So it's deeply disturbing that there are politicians peddling conspiracy theories out there and casting doubt on vaccinations when it is our best tool against the virus
sentences.zh: 因此，政客们在外面散布阴谋论，对疫苗接种提出质疑，这令人深感不安，因为疫苗是我们对抗病毒的最佳工具，

sentences.en: and the best tool to prevent even teenagers from being hospitalized.
sentences.zh: 也是防止青少年住院的最佳手段。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Rob Zipko, Rochelle Bonja, Chelsea Daniel, and Ricky Nowitzki.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由罗伯·齐普科、罗谢尔·邦贾、切尔西·丹尼尔和里基·诺维茨基制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Patricia Willans and Paige Cowett, contains original music by Dan Powell, and was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 由帕特里夏·威兰斯和佩奇·考维特编辑，包含丹·鲍威尔的原创音乐，并由克里斯·伍德负责工程制作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brunberg and Ben Lansford of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题曲由Wonderly乐队的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰斯福德创作。

sentences.en: Special thanks to Daniel Friedman.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢丹尼尔·弗里德曼。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Bavaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴瓦罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我，莎拉·凯尼格，将为你讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中逐渐失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在你收听播客的平台订阅收听。

sentences.en: Let's see you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们明天见。
